decisions.decision: Which rulings does this plan inherit from plans 1 and 2?
decisions.ruling: Keep the toml/ namespace. Credit the MIT code in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md plus a one-line source header in each ported file, test files included. Put the code in src/plugins/toml/. Dependencies follow the user's criterion (plan 2 D2): a direct dependency is not a concern; vendor what brings peer ranges or conflicting transitive trees. No Vue support (plan 2 D12). Each edit unit runs code:format --fix before it returns (plan 2 D17). @eslint/plugin-kit and @ota-meshi/ast-token-store are already direct dependencies from plan 2; debug is already direct.
decisions.rejected: A new namespace; a separate package; Vue support

decisions.decision: Which toml rules do we port?
decisions.ruling: 22 rules of eslint-plugin-toml 1.5.0: all except the Vue-only rule vue-custom-block/no-parsing-error and the deprecated rule space-eq-sign (replaced upstream by key-spacing).

decisions.decision: Which packages are kept and which are ported?
decisions.ruling: Remove eslint-plugin-toml (peer eslint >=9.38.0). Add toml-eslint-parser 1.0.3 as a direct, exact-pinned, bundled dependency: its one dependency is eslint-visitor-keys ^5.0.0 (ESLint pins ^5.0.1), and it has no peers.

decisions.decision: Which upstream source files are ported?
decisions.ruling: src/language/ (index.ts, toml-language.ts, toml-source-code.ts) to src/plugins/toml/language/; src/utils/ except rules.ts (ast-utils.ts, bit.ts, casing.ts, index.ts) to src/plugins/toml/utils/; src/types.ts and src/meta.ts. The group registries and the plugin index replace utils/rules.ts. Drop any part that exists only for Vue. JSON-schema types come from @eslint/core, never from json-schema. The language is registered as languages.toml, so its name stays toml/toml.
decisions.rejected: Port utils/rules.ts; keep the plugin for its language

decisions.decision: What test bar and which upstream tests?
decisions.ruling: A RuleTester test for each of the 22 rules, ported from tests/src/rules/<rule>.ts at tag v1.5.0 with the upstream config (plugins { toml: <plugin> }, language toml/toml) and the ported loader. U1 copies upstream tests/fixtures/rules/ byte for byte to tests/unit/plugins/toml/fixtures/rules/, without vue-custom-block/ and space-eq-sign/; integrations/ is not copied. The loader (tests/utils/utils.ts without makeSuiteTests and without vue-eslint-parser, and apply-fixer.ts) goes to tests/unit/plugins/toml/helpers/; loadTestCases takes the plugin object as a parameter and never writes a fixture (a missing errors or output file fails the test). U1 ports the language tests token-store, toml-language, toml-source-code and toml-source-code-with-core-rules, and tests/src/utils/casing.ts; cases that need a rule are left to U4. U4 ports tests/src/language/directive-comments.ts and those deferred cases into with-rules.test.ts, and tests/src/rules-without-vue-eslint-parser.ts into rules-on-js.test.ts. Not ported: toml-source-code-with-stylistic-rules (needs @stylistic/eslint-plugin), tests/src/meta.ts, tests/src/eslint-plugin.ts, tests/src/configs/, tests/src/utils/rules.ts, the vue-custom-block and space-eq-sign tests. Each test file connects RuleTester to vitest itself and imports from src/.
decisions.rejected: Golden snapshots only; port every upstream test

decisions.decision: Where does the rule configuration live, and how is parity proved?
decisions.ruling: In the toml preset. The plugin index (U4) exports meta, rules (merged from rules/group-a.ts and group-b.ts) and languages { toml }; no configs. The preset reproduces the recommended config of eslint-plugin-toml (language toml/toml, the core rules no-irregular-whitespace and spaced-comment off, and toml/no-unreadable-number-separator, toml/precision-of-fractional-seconds, toml/precision-of-integer as error), without toml/vue-custom-block/no-parsing-error, and keeps files ["**/*.toml"] (the same set as upstream's ["*.toml", "**/*.toml"]). After U4, lint/problems.json and lint/fixes.json do not change, and config/file.toml.json changes only by the removal of the toml/vue-custom-block/no-parsing-error entry; any other golden change stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: configs in the plugin; accept any golden change

decisions.ruling: One review unit after U4, because the change ships runnable code. Execution mode teams, because wave 2 has two edit units; if a team cannot start, the run uses solo.
MINOR: the Vue-only rule and the deprecated rule space-eq-sign are removed; no consumer config names either (scan of ~/Projects, 2026-11-22).

decisions.decision: What does a unit do when a ported upstream test fails only because ESLint 10 or vitest is stricter? (ruled by the user on 2026-11-22 for all B08 plans)
decisions.ruling: A ported upstream test case that fails only because ESLint 10's RuleTester or the vitest wiring is stricter than upstream's setup (jest on ESLint 9) — not because the rule behaves differently — may have its test setup changed: for example, remove a duplicate case, or add a property that ESLint 10 requires. Never change the expected messages, message ids, locations, output or suggestions. List each change as DECIDED; the review unit checks them. A case whose expected result differs stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: Stop and ask for each case; apply it to one plan only

decisions.decision: How are eslint-disable comments for unknown rules and strict-TypeScript errors in ported code handled?
decisions.ruling: (a) A ported file may drop an eslint-disable or eslint-enable comment that names a rule this repo does not define, or rewrite it to the rule of this repo that it means; ESLint 10 reports an unknown rule in such a comment as an error, so code:lint would fail. (b) Where the repo's strict TypeScript (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, .js import extensions) rejects ported code, a unit fixes it only with changes that have no runtime effect: non-null assertions, casts, type annotations, import type, and .js or /index.js on relative imports. No runtime guard is added. List each kind of change as DECIDED. (Ruled for all B08 plans on 2026-11-22, from the rulings review of plan 6.)
decisions.rejected: Define the unknown rules; add runtime guards
